Background

In the data folder, you will find data about shark incidents in California between 1950-2022. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

Load the libraries

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Load the data

Run the following code chunk to import the data. In this chunk, I am removing NA’s.

sharks <- 
  read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv", 
           na=c("NA", "N/A", "Unknown", "NOT COUNTED", "", " ")) %>% 
  clean_names()

Questions

  1. Are there any “hotspots” for shark incidents in California? Show the top five counties with the most incidents.
sharks %>% 
  select(incident_num, county) %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarise(county_inc= sum(incident_num, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(county_inc)) %>% 
  slice_head(n=5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   county        county_inc
##   <chr>              <dbl>
## 1 Santa Barbara       2546
## 2 San Diego           2431
## 3 Humboldt            1976
## 4 San Mateo           1750
## 5 Santa Cruz          1691
  1. Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents per county.
sharks %>% 
  select(incident_num, county) %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarise(county_inc= sum(incident_num, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=county, y=county_inc))+
  geom_col()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title = "number of incidents per county", x="number of incidents", y="county")

  1. Are there months of the year when incidents are more likely to occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by month. Which month has the highest number of incidents?
sharks_month <- sharks %>% 
  select(month, incident_num) %>% 
  mutate(month_name= month(month, label = T, abbr = F))
sharks_month %>% 
  group_by(month_name) %>% 
  summarise(month_inc= sum(incident_num, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=month_name, y= month_inc))+
  geom_col()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title = "number of incidents per month", x="number of incidents", y="month")

  1. Is there a time of day when most attacks occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by time of day. Which time of day has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  select(time, incident_num) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(time)) %>% 
  group_by(time) %>% 
  summarise(inc_time= sum(incident_num, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=time, y=inc_time)) +
  geom_col()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title = "number of incidents by time of day", x="number of incidents", y="time")

  1. How do the number and types of injuries compare by county? Make a table that shows the number of injury types by county. Which county has the highest number incidents? (hint: your table should be in wide format)
sharks %>% 
  select(injury, county, incident_num) %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  count(injury) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = "injury",
              values_from = "n")
## # A tibble: 22 × 8
## # Groups:   county [22]
##    county                 minor  none major `minor*` `none*` fatal `major*`
##    <chr>                  <int> <int> <int>    <int>   <int> <int>    <int>
##  1 Del Norte                  2     1    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  2 Humboldt                   2     9     7        1       1    NA       NA
##  3 Island - Catalina          1     3    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  4 Island - Farallones       NA    NA     7       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  5 Island - San Miguel        2    NA     2       NA      NA     1       NA
##  6 Island - San Nicolas       1    NA    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  7 Island - Santa Barbara    NA    NA    NA       NA      NA    NA        1
##  8 Island - Santa Cruz        1     1    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA
##  9 Island - Santa Rosa       NA    NA     1       NA      NA    NA       NA
## 10 Los Angeles                6     2    NA       NA      NA     1        1
## # ℹ 12 more rows
  1. Use the table from #5 to make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by county.
sharks %>% 
  select(injury, county, incident_num) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=county))+
  geom_bar(aes(fill = injury))+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title = "number of incidents per county", x= "county", y="number of incidents")

  1. In the data, mode refers to a type of activity. Which activity is associated with the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  select(mode, incident_num) %>% 
  group_by(mode) %>% 
  summarise(mode_inc= sum(incident_num, na.rm=T)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(mode_inc))
## # A tibble: 8 × 2
##   mode                mode_inc
##   <chr>                  <dbl>
## 1 Surfing / Boarding      9474
## 2 Kayaking / Canoeing     4317
## 3 Freediving              2501
## 4 Swimming                1816
## 5 Scuba Diving            1332
## 6 Paddleboarding           980
## 7 Hookah Diving            550
## 8 Walking in shallow         0
  1. Make a plot that compares the number of incidents by activity.
sharks %>% 
  select(mode, incident_num) %>% 
  count(mode, sort = T) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mode, y=n))+
  geom_col(aes(fill = mode))+
  labs(title = "Number of incidents per activity mode", x="activity mode", y="number of incidents")+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1))

  1. Which shark species is involved in the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  select(incident_num, species) %>% 
  group_by(species) %>% 
  summarise(species_inc= sum(incident_num, na.rm=T)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(species_inc)) %>% 
  slice_head()
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   species species_inc
##   <chr>         <dbl>
## 1 White         18374
  1. Are all incidents involving Great White’s fatal? Make a plot that shows the number and types of incidents for Great White’s only.
sharks %>% 
  filter(species=="White") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=injury))+
  geom_bar(aes(fill = injury))+
  labs(title = "number of incidents and type of injury by Great White sharks", x="injury type", y="number of incidents")
